topology_invariants.statement: Offline, peer-hosted browser and dedicated-authoritative modes consume byte-identical canonical creation content.
ThingId, DefinitionId, AttachmentId and PortId remain topology-independent.
Topology is runtime policy/context and does not create network-only Thing subclasses or authored rewrites.
Containment, controller binding, simulation authority and replication/relevance remain distinct relationships.
Client input is declared intent; a non-authority cannot assert authoritative replicated state.
Accepted equivalent input sequences reach the same authoritative semantic outcome across topologies.
State sequencing prevents stale delivery from rolling back current authoritative values.
Reliable logical events carry deduplication identity above transport delivery.
Relevance leave does not imply unload, destruction, containment change or authority transfer.
Known-unloaded Things retain bounded coalesced state and reliable event obligations until restore.
Reconnect preserves durable principal/Thing semantics while changing transient transport identity.
Peer authority migration requires a confirmed checkpoint and increments authority epoch.
Old-epoch messages are rejected after authority migration.
Peer host loss without confirmed checkpoint fails explicitly rather than electing from unconfirmed state.
Dedicated authority loss fails closed and does not promote an ordinary browser client.
Ingress recursively rejects serialized capability grants, host handles and engine identity.
Ingress enforces bounded message size and declared input/state/event loci independently.

Browser lifecycle behavior is measured in a real exported Chromium runtime and reported independently from reconnect fault injection; whether lifecycle naturally drops the transport and the actual reconnect trigger are recorded explicitly.
Peer-hosted and dedicated modes may differ in fairness/trust policy without changing canonical object semantics.
Topology projection, replication, reconnect and migration preserve the complete protected AssetId digest/source/audio/provenance/licence/derivation revision bundle.

exported browser peer authority and browser participant reach equivalent authoritative semantics
exported Linux dedicated authority plus browser client reaches equivalent authoritative semantics
unloaded event/state and relevance coalescing are observed in exported browser runtime

real browser lifecycle behavior is measured without assuming it drops the transport, then reconnect semantics are observed after the recorded natural or explicitly injected transport-loss trigger with changed transient connection identity
confirmed peer migration increments authority epoch and rejects injected prior-epoch input
unconfirmed peer host loss reports checkpoint_unconfirmed
dedicated server loss reports fail-closed and leaves no promoted browser authority
complete protected media bundle and canonical digest compare equal across normalized snapshots
